title: Chapter 286: What Is He Digging?
html:
Inspector Lee seemed reluctant to discuss the matter. Footsteps sounded over the line as he moved somewhere more private. “The child has a deeply distorted understanding of death.”

After meeting Men Nan’s primary personality, even the strangest child seemed normal to Chen Ge. “At that age, a child’s worldview is still developing. She might see death as a journey somewhere far away. I can understand that.”

“If only that were all. For three days after her rescue, the girl didn’t say a word. She neither protested nor cried. She was so obedient it became unsettling.” Inspector Lee recalled the case. “Things changed on the fourth day. A female officer found her curled in a corner of the bed, staring blankly at a spider. Thinking the child was terrified, the officer killed it. The girl burst into tears and accused her of killing her big sister.

“Those were the first words she spoke, and that was when we realized something was wrong. She showed no grief over her parents’ deaths, yet mourned a spider as if her world had ended. What kind of reality was she living in?

“When we tried explaining death, we discovered that she didn’t consider it an ending. With complete sincerity, she told us that people become something else after they die. It resembled a belief in reincarnation. Because death held no fear for her, brutal statements came easily from her lips.

“A cute girl that looked as innocent as an angel using her childish tone to talk about death. Is she an angel or a demon?

“Further investigation uncovered more troubling details. A passing villager reported the deaths. According to the autopsies, the girl had lived beside her parents’ bodies for at least two days before anyone found her.” Inspector Lee lowered his voice. “A five-year-old can think for herself, yet she neither called for help nor sought another adult for two entire days. Don’t you find that strange?”

“Perhaps her parents never taught her what to do in an emergency.” Jiang Ling’s pitiful face surfaced in Chen Ge’s mind, though even he now sensed that something about her was unusual.

“There were only the girl and her parents’ fingerprints inside the house. The method of killing was direct, but it was surprisingly successful. There were many other anomalies. In any case, this case is not as simple as you think.”

Someone called Inspector Lee’s name, and he answered. “Chen Ge, I have to go. I know I can’t stop you, but heed this warning: be careful around that child, and do not visit the village at night.”

“Why not?”

“Look at a map. Don’t you find it strange that nothing stands within miles of the village? During the investigation, we interviewed residents of the nearest settlement—which practically lies in another district. An elder there claimed that an epidemic once swept through Lin Guan Village and killed many people.” Someone urged Inspector Lee to hurry. After repeating his warning, he ended the call, leaving Chen Ge alone in the dark, abandoned village.

Chen Ge pocketed his phone. He said some time ago; how many years ago was that?

The village’s squat, rectangular houses resembled coffins. Even its name felt ominous: with one stroke removed from the character for “Lin,” Lin Guan Village became Mu Guan Village—Coffin Village.

He left the village and stopped beside the asphalt road. Finding a taxi there would have been difficult in broad daylight; at midnight, it was impossible. He had no way back to the city.

Jiang Ling said that her father’s peach plantation is to the western side of the village. I should go take a look.

Chen Ge switched on his flashlight and followed the road west. It narrowed as he traveled. After climbing a low hill, just as he was about to abandon the search, he spotted a light ahead.

Someone’s there?The light drifted deeper into the mountains, apparently unaware of him. Chen Ge pulled the hammer farther from his backpack and tucked Xiaoxiao into his breast pocket before following. The rocky trail forced him to move carefully. After ten minutes, the light slowly vanished.

Wait… Could it be spirit fire?!

Alone in the mountains, he remembered childhood ghost stories about wandering lights that lured innocent travelers deep into the wilderness.

Stay calm.Chen Ge slapped his cheeks, tightened his jacket, and jogged in the light’s direction. Rounding a hill, he discovered a peach orchard carved into the mountainside.

Neglect had allowed weeds to overrun the orchard and peach trees to lean at unnatural angles. From a distance, they resembled deformed human figures. The light reappeared among them.

This must be Jiang Ling’s father’s peach orchard.Finding it brought Chen Ge no relief. The mysterious light only heightened his tension.

Everyone nearby knows about the murder case in this village, so why would someone purposely come here in the middle of the night?Chen Ge moved cautiously. He switched off the flashlight. Thanks to his Yin Yang Vision, Chen Ge could see better than most in the dark.

He crept into the orchard. Soon, he heard the scrape of a tool biting into soil.

What is he doing?From nearby, Chen Ge could finally see clearly. A lamp hung from the branch of a peach tree. Beneath it, a man in his sixties dug through the orchard with a hoe as though searching for something. The strange behavior made Chen Ge remain silent and trail him from a distance.

Despite his crown of white hair, the man remained powerfully built. Thick calluses covered hands shaped by a lifetime of farm work. His faded shirt had nearly been washed colorless, and his taut face seemed incapable of smiling.

Just a normal old man…

By every outward measure, he was an ordinary elderly farmer. Why, then, was he digging at a murder scene in the middle of the night?

Afraid that appearing without warning might startle the old man, Chen Ge retreated several meters and switched on his flashlight before calling toward the orchard, “Is anyone there? How do I get out of these mountains?”

Even so, the voice from nowhere terrified the old man. Cold sweat instantly beaded across his forehead.
